1	"""Persistent storage: blockchain, pending set and derived indexes (JSON).
2	
3	The whole state is one JSON document written atomically: a uniquely named
4	``.ledger-*`` snapshot is fsynced in the same directory and then promoted over
5	the main file with ``os.replace`` (followed by a directory fsync). Every
6	successful write advances a monotonic ``generation`` recorded in the
7	snapshot. A crash can therefore only leave behind (a) the previous main file
8	or (b) a fully fsynced snapshot that never got renamed — never a torn file.
9	
10	On startup the main file and every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
11	as recovery candidates. When no file exists at all, the unique genesis block
12	is created; otherwise each candidate is strictly validated (JSON, generation,
13	consecutive heights, prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and Merkle
14	roots, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signature, pending-only-at-tip and
15	mempool/chain de-duplication). The valid snapshot with the highest generation
16	wins and is promoted if it is still a temp file; same-generation content
17	conflicts, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise StateRecoveryError
18	with the offending path and reason — a fresh chain is never silently created.
19	
20	One atomic write persists everything: the chain (each block carries its
21	confirm/rollback ``status``), a small ``state`` summary, the mempool
22	(``pending``), candidate fork chains (``forks``, each a full block list
23	anchored at the canonical genesis and keyed by its tip hash), the
24	confirmed-transaction ``index`` and the confirmed ``accounts`` activity.
25	Derived data (index/accounts) is *rebuilt* from the chain on every load and
26	every save — pending blocks are excluded, so a restart never resurrects
27	unconfirmed transactions into balances. Persisted fork candidates are
28	re-validated on startup and invalid ones are dropped, while canonical-chain
29	invalidity remains fatal. Each surviving sync record carries the tip summary
30	(height/length/status) frozen at reception; a persisted frozen summary that
31	disagrees with the re-resolved candidate invalidates the record, while a
32	snapshot predating the feature is repaired from its candidate. Persisted sync
33	records are re-verified on restart:
34	records still unexpired whose source stays active and unexpired survive;
35	records whose own deadline elapsed or whose source is unknown/revoked/
36	registry-expired while the process was down are pruned (their non-adopted
37	forks removed; an adopted tip never changes the canonical chain) and each
38	gets exactly one sync_expired audit event backfilled after the durable
39	history, persisted in one atomic write. The backfill deduplicates only
40	within the record's current lifecycle (a durable sync_expired newer than
41	the key's latest sync_received), so a reused (source, request_id) key's
42	new lifecycle is always audited even when every field matches a previous
43	lifecycle's event. Other staleness (a dangling
44	tip or a content-fingerprint mismatch) is a silent prune with no event.
45	A re-entrant lock serializes all updates, and a class-wide recovery lock
46	serializes startup scans against in-flight writes.
47	"""
48	from __future__ import annotations

51	import json
52	import os
53	import tempfile

55	import time

84	# the main state file. They double as crash-recovery candidates on startup.
85	SNAPSHOT_PREFIX = ".ledger-"

93	class SyncSummary:
94	    """Resolve the frozen tip descriptor (height/length/status) for a synced
95	    candidate during recovery, from either a surviving fork or a canonical
96	    chain prefix.
97	    """
98	
99	    @staticmethod
100	    def from_blocks_raw(tip_hash: str, blocks_raw: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
101	        """Build the descriptor for an already-resolved raw block list whose
102	        last block hash must equal ``tip_hash``.
103	        """
104	        if not blocks_raw:
105	            return None
106	        tip = blocks_raw[-1]
107	        if tip.get("block_hash") != tip_hash:
108	            return None
109	        return {
110	            "height": tip["height"],
111	            "length": len(blocks_raw),
112	            "status": tip["status"],
113	        }

115	    @classmethod
116	    def from_locations(
117	        cls,
118	        tip_hash: str,
119	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
120	        canonical_chain: list[Block],
121	    ) -> dict | None:
122	        """Resolve a descriptor among surviving forks first, then canonical
123	        blocks (the delivered fork may since have been adopted).
124	        """
125	        fork = forks.get(tip_hash)
126	        if fork is not None:
127	            return cls.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, [block.to_dict() for block in fork])
128	        prefix: list[dict] = []
129	        for block in canonical_chain:
130	            prefix.append(block.to_dict())
131	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
132	                return cls.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, prefix)
133	        return None

136	class StateRecoveryError(ValueError):
137	    """Raised when no usable on-disk state can be recovered on startup.
138	
139	    Carries the candidate ``path`` that failed and a human-readable ``reason``
140	    so callers can report (or catch) the failure explicitly. The exception is a
141	    ``ValueError`` subclass, so older callers expecting ``ValueError`` on a
142	    corrupt state file keep working.
143	    """
144	
145	    def __init__(self, path: str, reason: str) -> None:
146	        self.path = path
147	        self.reason = reason
148	        super().__init__(f"cannot recover ledger state from {path}: {reason}")

151	class LedgerStore:
152	    def __init__(self, path: str, initial_balance: int | None = None) -> None:
153	        self.path = path
154	        self.chain: list[Block] = []
155	        self.pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
156	        # Candidate fork chains keyed by tip block hash. Each value is the
157	        # fork's full block list (including the shared genesis block).
158	        self.forks: dict[str, list[Block]] = {}
159	        # Inter-node sync submissions keyed by (source, request_id). Each
160	        # record stores delivery metadata plus the tip hash of the synced
161	        # candidate chain (kept in ``forks``) and a content fingerprint used
162	        # for same-key retry/idempotency checks.
163	        self.syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
164	        # Persistent source-trust registry keyed by source identifier. Each
165	        # record is {"public_key", "expires_at", "version", "status"}.
166	        self.trust_sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
167	        # Keyless trust allowlist {source: expires_at}; preserved verbatim and
168	        # surfaced by GET /v1/trust for offline light clients.
169	        self.allowlist: dict[str, int] = {}
170	        # Append-only audit events, each {"event_id", "kind", "at",
171	        # "prev_hash", "event_hash", ...payload}. event_id is the 1-based
172	        # position in this list; the two hash fields form a SHA-256 chain
173	        # anchored at 64 zeroes.
174	        self.audit_events: list[dict] = []
175	        # Head of the audit hash chain: {"event_id", "event_hash"} of the last
176	        # event, or {0, "0"*64} for an empty log. Persisted in every snapshot.
177	        self.audit_checkpoint: dict = audit.make_checkpoint([])
178	        # Per-identity endowment used for candidate replay checks; recorded in
179	        # the snapshot so recovery validates against the same convention.
180	        self.initial_balance: int | None = initial_balance
181	        # Monotonic counter bumped on every successful atomic write. It is
182	        # persisted with each snapshot and lets startup pick the newest one.
183	        self.generation: int = 0
184	        # Derived, confirmed-only views; rebuilt by rebuild_derived().
185	        self.tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
186	        self.accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
187	        self._lock = threading.RLock()

189	
190	    @property
191	    def lock(self) -> threading.RLock:
192	        return self._lock
193	
194	    # Serializes startup scans/promotions between threads (or two store
195	    # instances on the same path) within one process. All later mutations take
196	    # the per-store re-entrant lock.
197	    _recovery_lock = threading.RLock()
198	
199	    def load(self) -> None:
200	        """Recover state from disk on startup.
201	
202	        The main file *and* every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
203	        as recovery candidates. When none exist at all, the unique genesis
204	        block is created (the established first-start convention); otherwise
205	        every candidate is strictly validated and the valid snapshot with the
206	        highest generation wins. A winning temp snapshot is atomically
207	        promoted over the main file and every judged-older or residual
208	        candidate is removed. Same-generation snapshots with conflicting
209	        content, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise
210	        StateRecoveryError — a fresh chain is never silently created.
211	        """
212	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
213	        with self._recovery_lock:
214	            candidates = self._discover_candidates(directory)
215	            if not candidates:
216	                os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
217	                self.chain = [self.create_genesis()]
218	                self.pending = {}
219	                self.forks = {}
220	                self.syncs = {}
221	                self.trust_sources = {}
222	                self.allowlist = {}
223	                self.audit_events = []
224	                self.audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint([])
225	                self.generation = 0
226	                self.rebuild_derived()
227	                self.save()
228	                return
229	
230	            valid: list[tuple] = []
231	            errors: list[StateRecoveryError] = []
232	            for candidate in candidates:
233	                try:
234	                    data = self._read_candidate(candidate)
235	                    parsed = self._parse_snapshot(candidate, data)
236	                except StateRecoveryError as exc:
237	                    errors.append(exc)
238	                    continue
239	                # parsed = (chain, pending, generation, forks, initial_balance,
240	                #           syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
241	                #           expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair)
242	                valid.append(
243	                    (
244	                        parsed[2],
245	                        candidate,
246	                        parsed[0],
247	                        parsed[1],
248	                        parsed[3],
249	                        parsed[4],
250	                        parsed[5],
251	                        parsed[6],
252	                        parsed[7],
253	                        parsed[8],
254	                        parsed[9],
255	                        parsed[10],
256	                        parsed[11],
257	                    )
258	                )

261	                details = "; ".join(f"{exc.path} ({exc.reason})" for exc in errors)
262	                raise StateRecoveryError(
263	                    directory, f"no valid snapshot candidate found: {details}"
264	                )
265	
266	            max_generation = max(item[0] for item in valid)
267	            top = [item for item in valid if item[0] == max_generation]
268	            # item layout: (generation, path, chain, pending, forks,
269	            # initial_balance, syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
270	            # expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair)
271	            reference = self._canonical_view(
272	                top[0][2],
273	                top[0][3],
274	                top[0][4],
275	                top[0][6],
276	                top[0][7],
277	                top[0][8],

279	                top[0][5],
280	                top[0][11],
281	            )

284	                    self._canonical_view(

286	                        item[3],
287	                        item[4],
288	                        item[6],
289	                        item[7],
290	                        item[8],
291	                        item[9],
292	                        item[5],
293	                        item[11],
294	                    )

299	                        directory,
300	                        f"conflicting snapshots at generation {max_generation}: {paths}",
301	                    )
302	
303	            # Identical same-generation snapshots: keep the main file when it
304	            # is one of them, avoiding a pointless promotion cycle.
305	            main_abs = os.path.abspath(self.path)
306	            winner = top[0]
307	            for item in top:
308	                if os.path.abspath(item[1]) == main_abs:

314	                chain,
315	                pending,

318	                syncs,

347	            if audit_repair or backfilled:

351	            self.pending = pending
352	            self.forks = forks
353	            self.syncs = syncs
354	            self.trust_sources = trust_sources
355	            self.allowlist = allowlist
356	            self.audit_events = audit_events

368	            # events + legacy hash-chain completion) atomically so the next
369	            # restart never re-derives or duplicates anything; with nothing to
370	            # reconcile no write happens and the recovered generation is kept
371	            # byte-for-byte.

375	    def _discover_candidates(self, directory: str) -> list[str]:
376	        """List the main file and sibling .ledger-* snapshots (if any)."""
377	        candidates: list[str] = []
378	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
379	            candidates.append(self.path)
380	        try:
381	            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory))
382	        except OSError:
383	            return candidates
384	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
385	        for name in names:
386	            if name == main_name or not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX):
387	                continue
388	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
389	            if os.path.isfile(full):
390	                candidates.append(full)
391	        return candidates
392	
393	    @staticmethod
394	    def _canonical_view(
395	        chain: list[Block],
396	        pending: dict[str, Transaction],
397	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
398	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None,
399	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
400	        allowlist: dict[str, int] | None = None,
401	        audit_events: list[dict] | None = None,
402	        initial_balance: int | None = None,
403	        audit_checkpoint: dict | None = None,
404	    ) -> str:
405	        """Order-independent canonical content hash for conflict detection.
406	
407	        The recorded ``initial_balance`` is part of the authoritative view: two
408	        same-generation snapshots with identical chains but a different
409	        endowment describe a different replay judgment and must conflict. The
410	        audit checkpoint participates too: two same-generation snapshots with
411	        the same events but a different log head disagree about the audited
412	        state and must conflict.
413	        """
414	        sync_records = [
415	            {
416	                "source": key[0],
417	                "request_id": key[1],
418	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
419	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
420	                "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
421	                "height": rec.get("height"),
422	                "length": rec.get("length"),
423	                "status": rec.get("status"),
424	            }
425	            for key, rec in sorted((syncs or {}).items())
426	        ]
427	        trust_records = [
428	            {"source": source, **rec}
429	            for source, rec in sorted((trust_sources or {}).items())
430	        ]
431	        return json.dumps(
432	            {
433	                "initial_balance": initial_balance,
434	                "chain": [block.to_dict() for block in chain],
435	                "pending": [pending[tx_id].to_dict() for tx_id in sorted(pending)],
436	                "forks": [
437	                    [block.to_dict() for block in forks[tip]]
438	                    for tip in sorted(forks)
439	                ],
440	                "syncs": sync_records,
441	                "trust_sources": trust_records,
442	                "allowlist": dict(sorted((allowlist or {}).items())),
443	                "audit_events": audit_events or [],
444	                "audit_checkpoint": audit_checkpoint
445	                or {"event_id": 0, "event_hash": "0" * 64},
446	            },
447	            sort_keys=True,
448	            ensure_ascii=False,
449	        )

451	    def _cleanup_candidates(self, directory: str) -> None:
452	        """Remove every residual .ledger-* snapshot next to the main file.
453	
454	        After recovery these are by definition unusable leftovers: older
455	        generations, an identical post-promotion residue, or a partially
456	        written (invalid) file. The promoted/main state is never touched.
457	        """
458	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
459	        for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
460	            if not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX) or name == main_name:
461	                continue
462	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
463	            try:
464	                if os.path.isfile(full) or os.path.islink(full):
465	                    os.unlink(full)
466	            except OSError:
467	                pass
468	        self._fsync_dir(directory)

471	    def _read_candidate(path: str) -> dict:
472	        """Read and JSON-decode one snapshot file.
473	
474	        Any I/O or JSON failure becomes a StateRecoveryError carrying the
475	        offending path, never a silent fall-back.
476	        """
477	        try:
478	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
479	                data = json.load(fh)
480	        except OSError as exc:
481	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"cannot read file: {exc}") from exc
482	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
483	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
484	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
485	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "snapshot root must be a JSON object")
486	        return data

488	    def _parse_snapshot(
489	        self, path: str, data: dict
490	    ) -> tuple[
491	        list[Block],
492	        dict[str, Transaction],
493	        int,
494	        dict[str, list[Block]],
495	        int | None,
496	        dict[tuple[str, str], dict],
497	        dict[str, dict],
498	        dict[str, int],
499	        list[dict],
500	        list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
501	        dict,
502	        bool,
503	    ]:
504	        """Strictly validate one decoded snapshot.
505	
506	        Checks the persisted generation, consecutive heights, prev_hash
507	        linkage, recomputed block hashes, recomputed Merkle roots, every
508	        transaction's tx_id and Ed25519 signature, the pending-only-at-tip
509	        rule, and de-duplication between mempool and chain. Returns the parsed
510	        chain, mempool, generation, candidate forks and the recorded initial
511	        balance. Raises StateRecoveryError on the first defect, with ``path``
512	        identifying the candidate.
513	        """
514	        def fail(reason: str) -> None:
515	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, reason)
516	
517	        chain_raw = data.get("chain")
518	        if not isinstance(chain_raw, list) or not chain_raw:
519	            fail("snapshot must contain a non-empty chain")
520	
521	        state = data.get("state")
522	        # A pre-state-section snapshot is accepted: the chain itself is fully
523	        # self-verifying below. A present non-object section is corruption.
524	        if state is None:
525	            state = {}
526	        if not isinstance(state, dict):
527	            fail("invalid 'state' section: must be a JSON object")
528	        generation = state.get("generation", 0)
529	        # bool is an int subclass; reject it explicitly along with negatives.
530	        if isinstance(generation, bool) or not isinstance(generation, int) or generation < 0:
531	            fail("state.generation must be a non-negative integer")
532	        initial_balance = state.get("initial_balance")
533	        if initial_balance is not None and (
534	            isinstance(initial_balance, bool)
535	            or not isinstance(initial_balance, int)
536	            or initial_balance <= 0
537	        ):
538	            fail("state.initial_balance must be a positive integer")
539	
540	        chain: list[Block] = []
541	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
542	        for i, block_raw in enumerate(chain_raw):
543	            if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
544	                fail(f"block at position {i} is not a JSON object")
545	            try:
546	                block = Block.from_dict(block_raw)
547	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
548	                fail(f"block {i} is malformed: {exc}")
549	            if block.height != i:
550	                fail(
551	                    f"block at position {i} has non-consecutive height "
552	                    f"{block.height}"
553	                )
554	            expected_prev = GENESIS_PREV_HASH if i == 0 else chain[i - 1].block_hash
555	            if block.prev_hash != expected_prev:
556	                fail(f"block {block.height} has a mismatched prev_hash")
557	            if block.status not in (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED):
558	                fail(f"block {block.height} has unknown status {block.status!r}")
559	            if i == 0 and (
560	                block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.transactions
561	            ):
562	                fail("genesis block must be confirmed and carry no transactions")
563	            # Pending blocks may only sit at the chain tip.
564	            if i < len(chain_raw) - 1 and block.status == STATUS_PENDING:
565	                fail(f"pending block {block.height} is not the chain tip")
566	
567	            # Validate every transaction: stored tx_id, recomputed tx_id and
568	            # the Ed25519 signature.
569	            tx_ids: list[str] = []
570	            txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
571	            if not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
572	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions must be a list")
573	            for j, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
574	                self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
575	                stored_tx_id = txs_raw[j].get("tx_id") if isinstance(txs_raw[j], dict) else None
576	                if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id:
577	                    fail(
578	                        f"transaction in block {block.height} has a mismatched "
579	                        f"tx_id (stored {stored_tx_id!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
580	                    )
581	                if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
582	                    fail(
583	                        f"duplicate transaction {tx.tx_id} in block "
584	                        f"{block.height}"
585	                    )
586	                seen_tx_ids.add(tx.tx_id)
587	                tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)
588	            # Blocks store transactions in ascending tx_id order.
589	            if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
590	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions are not tx_id sorted")
591	
592	            recomputed_merkle = crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids)
593	            if recomputed_merkle != block.merkle_root:
594	                fail(f"block {block.height} Merkle root mismatch")
595	            recomputed_hash = compute_block_hash(
596	                block.height, block.prev_hash, block.merkle_root
597	            )
598	            if recomputed_hash != block.block_hash:
599	                fail(f"block {block.height} block_hash mismatch")
600	            chain.append(block)
601	
602	        # Mempool: well-formed, no internal duplicates, never overlapping the
603	        # chain (neither confirmed nor pending-block transactions).
604	        pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
605	        pending_raw = data.get("pending", [])
606	        if not isinstance(pending_raw, list):
607	            fail("'pending' must be a list")
608	        for tx_raw in pending_raw:
609	            if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
610	                fail("pending entry is not a JSON object")
611	            try:
612	                tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
613	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
614	                fail(f"pending transaction is malformed: {exc}")
615	            self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
616	            if tx_raw.get("tx_id") != tx.tx_id:
617	                fail(
618	                    f"pending transaction has a mismatched tx_id (stored "
619	                    f"{tx_raw.get('tx_id')!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
620	                )
621	            if tx.tx_id in pending:
622	                fail(f"duplicate pending transaction {tx.tx_id} in mempool")
623	            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
624	                fail(
625	                    f"pending transaction {tx.tx_id} already exists in a block"
626	                )
627	            pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
628	
629	        # Cross-check the persisted tip summary against the chain tail.
630	        tip = chain[-1]
631	        if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
632	            fail("state.height does not match the chain tip")
633	        if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
634	            fail("state.tip_hash does not match the chain tip")
635	        if (
636	            state.get("tip_status") is not None
637	            and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
638	        ):
639	            fail("state.tip_status does not match the chain tip")
640	
641	        # The recorded endowment is the *only* balance-replay parameter for the
642	        # persisted fork candidates: revalidation below must use it rather than
643	        # this instance's constructor argument, so starting with a different
644	        # --initial-balance can never change a fork's legality. Only a legacy
645	        # snapshot that records no endowment falls back to the configured (then
646	        # the default) value; every snapshot written by current code records it.
647	        replay_endowment = initial_balance
648	        if replay_endowment is None:
649	            replay_endowment = (
650	                self.initial_balance
651	                if self.initial_balance is not None
652	                else DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
653	            )
654	
655	        forks = self._parse_persisted_forks(
656	            data.get("forks", []), chain, replay_endowment
657	        )
658	        # The trust registry is authoritative configuration and must be parsed
659	        # before the sync records, whose sources are re-authorized against it.
660	        trust_sources = self._parse_persisted_trust_sources(
661	            data.get("trust_sources", []), path
662	        )
663	        # Parse the durable append-only audit log verbatim. It must NOT be
664	        # mutated here: same-generation snapshot conflict detection compares
665	        # parsed audit events, and a time-dependent backfill would make two
666	        # byte-identical snapshots look conflicting. The expired-record
667	        # reconciliation returned below is applied once, by load(), to the
668	        # single winning snapshot.
669	        audit_events = self._parse_persisted_audit_events(
670	            data.get("audit_events", []), path
671	        )
672	        audit_checkpoint, audit_repair = self._assess_audit_chain(
673	            data, audit_events, path
674	        )
675	        syncs, expired_records, synced_tips = self._parse_persisted_syncs(
676	            data.get("syncs", []), forks, chain, trust_sources
677	        )
678	        # A fork brought in only by a sync record loses its right to exist once
679	        # that record is gone (expired/unauthorized/invalid on restart):
680	        # without this, the independently-persisted fork would resurrect as a
681	        # never-expiring candidate. Direct submissions carry no sync record and
682	        # are untouched.
683	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in syncs.values()}
684	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in chain}
685	        for tip in synced_tips - live_tips - canonical_hashes:
686	            forks.pop(tip, None)
687	        allowlist = self._parse_persisted_allowlist(data.get("allowlist", {}), path)
688	        return (
689	            chain,
690	            pending,
691	            generation,
692	            forks,
693	            initial_balance,
694	            syncs,
695	            trust_sources,
696	            allowlist,
697	            audit_events,
698	            expired_records,
699	            audit_checkpoint,
700	            audit_repair,
701	        )

703	    @staticmethod
704	    def _assess_audit_chain(
705	        data: dict, audit_events: list[dict], path: str
706	    ) -> tuple[dict, bool]:
707	        """Validate the persisted audit hash chain and checkpoint.
708	
709	        Returns ``(checkpoint, needs_repair)``. Three cases:
710	
711	        * a current snapshot with complete hash links: every dense id,
712	          prev_hash link and event_hash is recomputed and the persisted
713	          ``audit_checkpoint`` must pin the exact log head — any mismatch is
714	          snapshot corruption and fails recovery;
715	        * a legacy snapshot predating hash chaining (no link fields, no
716	          checkpoint, or a checkpoint-less section): accepted for a one-time
717	          repair performed by load() on the unique winner; the checkpoint
718	          returned here is the would-be head so same-generation conflict
719	          comparison stays content-based;
720	        * a partially linked log or a present-but-mismatched checkpoint/link:
721	          corruption, never silently repaired.
722	        """
723	        linked_flags = [
724	            isinstance(event, dict)
725	            and ("prev_hash" in event or "event_hash" in event)
726	            for event in audit_events
727	        ]
728	        any_linked = any(linked_flags)
729	        all_linked = all(linked_flags)
730	        checkpoint_raw = data.get("audit_checkpoint")
731	        if any_linked and not all_linked:
732	            raise StateRecoveryError(
733	                path, "audit log is only partially hash-linked"
734	            )
735	        if all_linked and (audit_events or checkpoint_raw is not None):
736	            # A linked log (or an empty log already carrying a checkpoint) is
737	            # strictly verified: links recompute and the checkpoint must pin
738	            # the exact log head.
739	            try:
740	                audit.validate_event_chain(audit_events)
741	            except audit.AuditChainError as exc:
742	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, exc.reason) from exc
743	            if checkpoint_raw is None:
744	                raise StateRecoveryError(
745	                    path, "hash-linked audit log is missing audit_checkpoint"
746	                )
747	            try:
748	                audit.validate_checkpoint(checkpoint_raw, audit_events)
749	            except audit.AuditChainError as exc:
750	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, exc.reason) from exc
751	            return dict(checkpoint_raw), False
752	        # Legacy unlinked log (including a pre-feature empty log with no
753	        # checkpoint). A present checkpoint is inconsistent with an unlinked
754	        # log: treat as corruption rather than silently ignoring it.
755	        if checkpoint_raw is not None:
756	            raise StateRecoveryError(
757	                path, "audit_checkpoint present on an unlinked audit log"
758	            )
759	        linked = audit.link_events(audit_events)
760	        return audit.make_checkpoint(linked), True

762	    @staticmethod
763	    def _backfill_expired_events(
764	        audit_events: list[dict],
765	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
766	    ) -> int:
767	        """Append one sync_expired event per down-time-expired sync record.
768	
769	        Mirrors the runtime sweep exactly: records are processed in
770	        ``(source, request_id)`` order, each gets a dense event_id continuing
771	        after the durable history, and every *lifecycle removal* gets its own
772	        event. Deduplication is lifecycle-aware, never identity-based across
773	        lifecycles: a durable sync_expired covers the persisted record only
774	        when it sits after the latest sync_received for the same
775	        ``(source, request_id)`` key — i.e. it belongs to the record's
776	        current lifecycle (the crash-interrupted-cleanup case). An expiry
777	        event from an *earlier* lifecycle of a reused key never suppresses
778	        the new lifecycle's event, even when source, request_id, tip_hash
779	        and expires_at are all identical. Returns the number of events
780	        appended. Mutates ``audit_events`` in place.
781	        """
782	        # Position of the latest sync_received per key: it opens the
783	        # lifecycle every later event of that key belongs to.
784	        last_received: dict[tuple[object, object], int] = {}
785	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
786	            if event.get("kind") == EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED:
787	                last_received[(event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))] = index
788	        # Identities already expired *within their current lifecycle*.
789	        covered: set[tuple[object, object, object]] = set()
790	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
791	            if event.get("kind") != EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED:
792	                continue
793	            key = (event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))
794	            if index > last_received.get(key, -1):
795	                covered.add((key[0], key[1], event.get("tip_hash")))
796	        backfilled = 0
797	        for source, request_id, rec in sorted(
798	            expired_records, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1])
799	        ):
800	            identity = (source, request_id, rec["tip_hash"])
801	            if identity in covered:
802	                continue
803	            event = {
804	                "event_id": len(audit_events) + 1,
805	                "kind": EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
806	                "at": time.time(),
807	                "source": source,
808	                "request_id": request_id,
809	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
810	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
811	            }
812	            # Freeze the delivered summary when recovery could resolve it;
813	            # records in snapshots older than the frozen-summary feature may
814	            # not carry one, in which case the history query resolves live.
815	            if rec.get("height") is not None:
816	                event["height"] = rec["height"]
817	                event["length"] = rec.get("length")
818	                event["status"] = rec.get("status")
819	            audit_events.append(event)
820	            covered.add(identity)
821	            backfilled += 1
822	        return backfilled

824	    @staticmethod
825	    def _parse_persisted_trust_sources(
826	        raw: object, path: str
827	    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
828	        """Strictly parse the persisted source-trust registry.
829	
830	        Unlike candidate forks (re-validated and silently dropped when stale),
831	        the trust registry is authoritative configuration: a malformed entry
832	        is snapshot corruption and fails recovery rather than being dropped.
833	        Each record needs a non-empty source, a 64-char lowercase hex public
834	        key, an integer expiry, a positive integer version and a known status.
835	        """
836	        if raw is None:
837	            return {}
838	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
839	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'trust_sources' must be a list")
840	        sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
841	        for entry in raw:
842	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
843	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source entry must be an object")
844	            source = entry.get("source")
845	            public_key = entry.get("public_key")
846	            expires_at = entry.get("expires_at")
847	            version = entry.get("version")
848	            status = entry.get("status")
849	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
850	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source must be a non-empty string")
851	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
852	                raise StateRecoveryError(
853	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has an invalid public_key"
854	                )
855	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
856	                raise StateRecoveryError(
857	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
858	                )
859	            if (
860	                isinstance(version, bool)
861	                or not isinstance(version, int)
862	                or version < 1
863	            ):
864	                raise StateRecoveryError(
865	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} version must be a positive integer"
866	                )
867	            if status not in (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED):
868	                raise StateRecoveryError(
869	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has invalid status {status!r}"
870	                )
871	            if source in sources:
872	                raise StateRecoveryError(
873	                    path, f"duplicate trust source {source!r} in snapshot"
874	                )
875	            sources[source] = {
876	                "public_key": public_key,
877	                "expires_at": expires_at,
878	                "version": version,
879	                "status": status,
880	            }
881	        return sources
882	
883	    @staticmethod
884	    def _parse_persisted_allowlist(raw: object, path: str) -> dict[str, int]:
885	        """Strictly parse the keyless ``{source: expires_at}`` allowlist."""
886	        if raw is None:
887	            return {}
888	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
889	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'allowlist' must be a JSON object")
890	        allowlist: dict[str, int] = {}
891	        for source, expires_at in raw.items():
892	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
893	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "allowlist source must be a non-empty string")
894	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
895	                raise StateRecoveryError(
896	                    path, f"allowlist entry {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
897	                )
898	            allowlist[source] = expires_at
899	        return allowlist

901	    @staticmethod
902	    def _parse_persisted_audit_events(raw: object, path: str) -> list[dict]:
903	        """Strictly parse the append-only audit event log.
904	
905	        Every event is a JSON object carrying an integer ``at`` timestamp and a
906	        string ``kind``; ``event_id`` values must be exactly 1..N with no gaps
907	        or duplicates, since the id is the event's permanent audit position
908	        (which also fixes the log's total ordering). Payload fields beyond
909	        those three are retained verbatim.
910	
911	        The historical sync lifecycle events additionally have their provenance
912	        metadata validated: ``sync_received`` / ``sync_adopted`` /
913	        ``sync_expired`` must carry a non-empty ``source`` and ``request_id``
914	        and a 64-char lowercase hex ``tip_hash``; an ``expires_at`` and the
915	        frozen tip summary (``height`` / ``length`` / ``status``) are checked
916	        when present — older snapshots' adopted events predate those fields, so
917	        missing ones are accepted but malformed ones are corruption.
918	        """
919	        if raw is None:
920	            return []
921	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
922	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'audit_events' must be a list")
923	        sync_kinds = {
924	            EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED,
925	            EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED,
926	            EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
927	        }
928	        events: list[dict] = []
929	        for i, event in enumerate(raw):
930	            if not isinstance(event, dict):
931	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {i + 1} must be an object")
932	            event_id = event.get("event_id")
933	            kind = event.get("kind")
934	            at = event.get("at")
935	            if (
936	                isinstance(event_id, bool)
937	                or not isinstance(event_id, int)
938	                or event_id != i + 1
939	            ):
940	                raise StateRecoveryError(
941	                    path,
942	                    f"audit event at position {i} has event_id {event_id!r}, "
943	                    f"expected {i + 1}",
944	                )
945	            if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
946	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {event_id} needs a kind")
947	            if isinstance(at, bool) or not isinstance(at, (int, float)):
948	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {event_id} needs a numeric 'at'")
949	            if kind in sync_kinds:
950	                source = event.get("source")
951	                request_id = event.get("request_id")
952	                tip_hash = event.get("tip_hash")
953	                if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
954	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
955	                        path, f"audit event {event_id} ({kind}) needs a source"
956	                    )
957	                if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
958	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
959	                        path, f"audit event {event_id} ({kind}) needs a request_id"
960	                    )
961	                if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
962	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
963	                        path, f"audit event {event_id} ({kind}) has an invalid tip_hash"
964	                    )
965	                expires_at = event.get("expires_at")
966	                if expires_at is not None and (
967	                    isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int)
968	                ):
969	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
970	                        path,
971	                        f"audit event {event_id} ({kind}) expires_at must be an integer",
972	                    )
973	                height = event.get("height")
974	                if height is not None and (
975	                    isinstance(height, bool) or not isinstance(height, int) or height < 0
976	                ):
977	                    raise StateRecoveryError(

1008	    def _parse_persisted_syncs(
1009	        self,
1010	        syncs_raw: object,
1011	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
1012	        canonical_chain: list[Block],
1013	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
1014	    ) -> tuple[dict[tuple[str, str], dict], list[tuple[str, str, dict]], set[str]]:
1015	        """Parse persisted sync records, dropping unusable ones on restart.
1016	
1017	        A record is kept only when it is structurally valid, has not yet
1018	        expired, its source is still an active, unexpired entry of the
1019	        persistent trust registry, and its tip references either a surviving
1020	        candidate fork or a block on the canonical chain (a synced candidate
1021	        may have been adopted). Records that expire while the process is down,
1022	        or whose source is unknown/revoked/registry-expired, are pruned and
1023	        additionally returned as ``expired_records`` (each as
1024	        ``(source, request_id, {tip_hash, expires_at, fingerprint})``) so the
1025	        caller backfills one sync_expired audit event per record — mirroring
1026	        the runtime sweep. Other staleness (malformed structure, a record
1027	        pointing at neither surviving location, or a fingerprint that no
1028	        longer matches the delivered candidate) is a silent orphan prune with
1029	        no event; duplicated keys keep the first copy. Invalid records are
1030	        silently dropped rather than failing recovery of the canonical chain.
1031	        The historical sync_received/sync_adopted/sync_expired audit events
1032	        are never touched by this pruning. Also returns the set of every tip
1033	        any sync record claims provenance for (including dropped ones), so the
1034	        caller can drop forks that only a pruned sync kept alive.
1035	        """
1036	        if not isinstance(syncs_raw, list):
1037	            return {}, [], set()
1038	        now = time.time()
1039	        trust_sources = trust_sources or {}
1040	        # Map every canonical block hash to the chain prefix ending there:
1041	        # this is the exact "candidate" document that was delivered for a tip
1042	        # since adopted onto the canonical chain.
1043	        canonical_prefixes: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
1044	        prefix: list[dict] = []
1045	        for block in canonical_chain:
1046	            prefix = prefix + [block.to_dict()]
1047	            canonical_prefixes[block.block_hash] = prefix
1048	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
1049	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]] = []
1050	        synced_tips: set[str] = set()
1051	        for rec_raw in syncs_raw:
1052	            if not isinstance(rec_raw, dict):
1053	                continue
1054	            source = rec_raw.get("source")
1055	            request_id = rec_raw.get("request_id")
1056	            tip_hash = rec_raw.get("tip_hash")
1057	            expires_at = rec_raw.get("expires_at")
1058	            fingerprint = rec_raw.get("fingerprint")
1059	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1060	                continue
1061	            if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
1062	                continue
1063	            if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
1064	                continue
1065	            # The frozen tip summary is optional for snapshots written before
1066	            # it was persisted; when present it must be structurally sound.
1067	            frozen_height = rec_raw.get("height")
1068	            frozen_length = rec_raw.get("length")
1069	            frozen_status = rec_raw.get("status")
1070	            if frozen_height is not None and (
1071	                isinstance(frozen_height, bool)
1072	                or not isinstance(frozen_height, int)
1073	                or frozen_height < 0
1074	            ):
1075	                continue
1076	            if frozen_length is not None and (
1077	                isinstance(frozen_length, bool)
1078	                or not isinstance(frozen_length, int)
1079	                or frozen_length < 1
1080	            ):
1081	                continue
1082	            if frozen_status is not None and frozen_status not in (
1083	                STATUS_PENDING,
1084	                STATUS_CONFIRMED,
1085	            ):
1086	                continue
1087	            # Provenance is recorded even for dropped records: it proves the
1088	            # matching fork must not outlive the sync that delivered it.
1089	            synced_tips.add(tip_hash)
1090	            record = {
1091	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
1092	                "expires_at": expires_at,
1093	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
1094	                "height": frozen_height,
1095	                "length": frozen_length,
1096	                "status": frozen_status,
1097	            }
1098	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
1099	                # Malformed deadline: a structurally broken record, silently
1100	                # pruned (no lifecycle event is attributable to it).
1101	                continue
1102	            expired_deadline = expires_at <= now
1103	            # Re-authorization on restart: the trust decision recorded at
1104	            # delivery is re-checked against the current registry. A source
1105	            # rotated away, revoked or expired since then invalidates its
1106	            # pending records; historical audit events stay queryable.
1107	            trusted = trust_sources.get(source)
1108	            auth_ok = (
1109	                trusted is not None
1110	                and trusted.get("status") == TRUST_ACTIVE
1111	                and isinstance(trusted.get("expires_at"), int)
1112	                and not isinstance(trusted.get("expires_at"), bool)
1113	                and trusted["expires_at"] > now
1114	            )
1115	            if expired_deadline or not auth_ok:
1116	                # Deadline elapsed or authorization lost while down: reconcile
1117	                # exactly like the runtime sweep and backfill sync_expired,
1118	                # regardless of the content fingerprint (the lifecycle event
1119	                # is identified by source/request_id/tip/expires_at). Best
1120	                # effort: freeze the summary from the surviving candidate when
1121	                # the snapshot predates frozen summaries, so the backfilled
1122	                # history row stays truthfully ordered.
1123	                if frozen_height is None:
1124	                    descriptor = SyncSummary.from_locations(
1125	                        tip_hash, forks, canonical_chain
1126	                    )
1127	                    if descriptor is not None:
1128	                        record.update(descriptor)
1129	                expired_records.append((source, request_id, record))
1130	                continue
1131	            if not isinstance(fingerprint, str) or not fingerprint:
1132	                continue
1133	            # Re-resolve the delivered candidate (a surviving fork, or the
1134	            # canonical prefix for an adopted tip) and recompute its content
1135	            # fingerprint: a tampered tip summary, deadline or request body
1136	            # must not be trusted on the strength of the persisted record.
1137	            blocks_raw: list[dict] | None = None
1138	            surviving_fork = forks.get(tip_hash)
1139	            if surviving_fork is not None:
1140	                blocks_raw = [block.to_dict() for block in surviving_fork]
1141	            else:
1142	                blocks_raw = canonical_prefixes.get(tip_hash)
1143	            if blocks_raw is None:
1144	                continue
1145	            if self._candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw) != fingerprint:
1146	                continue
1147	            # Verify the frozen summary metadata against the re-resolved
1148	            # candidate: like a fingerprint mismatch, a tampered summary
1149	            # invalidates the record silently (no lifecycle event), while a
1150	            # legacy record without the frozen fields is repaired from the
1151	            # candidate it references.
1152	            descriptor = SyncSummary.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, blocks_raw)
1153	            if descriptor is None:
1154	                continue
1155	            if frozen_height is not None and (
1156	                frozen_height != descriptor["height"]
1157	                or frozen_length != descriptor["length"]
1158	                or frozen_status != descriptor["status"]
1159	            ):
1160	                continue
1161	            record.update(descriptor)
1162	            key = (source, request_id)
1163	            if key in syncs:
1164	                continue
1165	            syncs[key] = {
1166	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
1167	                "expires_at": expires_at,
1168	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
1169	                "height": descriptor["height"],
1170	                "length": descriptor["length"],
1171	                "status": descriptor["status"],
1172	            }
1173	        return syncs, expired_records, synced_tips

1175	    @staticmethod

1180	        the persisted record against the re-parsed candidate without importing
1181	        the service layer. Key order and whitespace are normalized.
1182	        """
1183	        return hashlib.sha256(
1184	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

1222	    def _compute_derived(self) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict]]:
1223	        """Build the confirmed-only transaction index and account activity.
1224	
1225	        Pending blocks are excluded: only confirmed blocks contribute to
1226	        balances and to the tx_id -> height index. Pure: it returns fresh
1227	        dicts and never mutates store state, so callers can compute a
1228	        prospective view and publish it only after a successful write.
1229	        """
1230	        tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
1231	        accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
1232	        for block in self.chain:
1233	            if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1234	                continue
1235	            for tx in block.transactions:
1236	                tx_index[tx.tx_id] = block.height
1237	                for account in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
1238	                    entry = accounts.setdefault(
1239	                        account, {"sent": 0, "received": 0, "transactions": []}
1240	                    )
1241	                    entry["transactions"].append(tx.tx_id)
1242	                accounts[tx.sender]["sent"] += tx.amount
1243	                accounts[tx.recipient]["received"] += tx.amount
1244	        return tx_index, accounts

1246	    def rebuild_derived(self) -> None:
1247	        """Rebuild the confirmed-only transaction index and account activity.
1248	
1249	        Pending blocks are excluded: only confirmed blocks contribute to
1250	        balances and to the tx_id -> height index.

1254	    def save(self) -> None:
1255	        """Atomically persist chain, state, pending set, index and accounts.
1256	
1257	        The new state is first written to a uniquely named ``.ledger-*``
1258	        snapshot in the same directory and force-fsynced; only after that does
1259	        an atomic ``os.replace`` promote it to the main file. A crash between
1260	        the fsync and the promotion leaves the snapshot behind, where the
1261	        startup scan finds it as a recovery candidate. The in-memory
1262	        ``generation`` is advanced only after the promotion succeeds, so every
1263	        *successful* atomic write corresponds to exactly one generation.
1264	        """
1265	        # Compute the prospective confirmed-only views WITHOUT publishing them:
1266	        # they describe the *post-write* chain and must not become visible in
1267	        # memory until the promotion succeeds. A failure anywhere below leaves
1268	        # ``self.tx_index``/``self.accounts`` describing the last durably
1269	        # committed chain, which is exactly the state the caller's own rollback
1270	        # restores the rest of the fields to.
1271	        next_index, next_accounts = self._compute_derived()
1272	        next_generation = self.generation + 1
1273	        # The in-memory log, its hash head and checkpoint always move together:
1274	        # refuse to persist a document where they disagree, since that could
1275	        # never recover. Callers append through append_audit_event(), which
1276	        # advances both atomically.
1277	        if self.audit_checkpoint != audit.make_checkpoint(self.audit_events):
1278	            raise RuntimeError(
1279	                "audit_checkpoint does not match the audit log head; refusing "
1280	                "to persist an inconsistent snapshot"
1281	            )
1282	        data = {
1283	            "state": {
1284	                "version": STATE_VERSION,
1285	                "generation": next_generation,
1286	                "height": self.chain[-1].height,
1287	                "tip_hash": self.chain[-1].block_hash,
1288	                "tip_status": self.chain[-1].status,
1289	                "initial_balance": self.initial_balance,
1290	            },
1291	            "chain": [block.to_dict() for block in self.chain],
1292	            "pending": [tx.to_dict() for tx in self.pending.values()],
1293	            "index": dict(next_index),
1294	            "accounts": next_accounts,
1295	            "audit_checkpoint": dict(self.audit_checkpoint),
1296	        }
1297	        # Only persist a forks section when candidates exist so a chain with
1298	        # no forks keeps the canonical snapshot layout; loads default to [].
1299	        if self.forks:
1300	            data["forks"] = [
1301	                [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
1302	                for fork in sorted(self.forks.values(), key=lambda f: f[-1].block_hash)
1303	            ]
1304	        # Sync metadata is persisted in the same atomic document as the
1305	        # candidate chains it references.
1306	        if self.syncs:
1307	            data["syncs"] = [
1308	                {
1309	                    "source": key[0],
1310	                    "request_id": key[1],
1311	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
1312	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
1313	                    "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
1314	                    "height": rec.get("height"),
1315	                    "length": rec.get("length"),
1316	                    "status": rec.get("status"),
1317	                }
1318	                for key, rec in sorted(self.syncs.items())
1319	            ]
1320	        # Persistent source-trust registry and the keyless allowlist are part
1321	        # of the same atomic document as every state change they describe.
1322	        if self.trust_sources:
1323	            data["trust_sources"] = [
1324	                {"source": source, **self.trust_sources[source]}
1325	                for source in sorted(self.trust_sources)
1326	            ]
1327	        if self.allowlist:
1328	            data["allowlist"] = dict(sorted(self.allowlist.items()))
1329	        # The audit trail is append-only; every trust change and every sync
1330	        # reception/adoption/expiry is recorded here in write order.
1331	        if self.audit_events:
1332	            data["audit_events"] = list(self.audit_events)
1333	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
1334	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
1335	        # Hold the class-wide recovery lock while a .ledger-* snapshot exists
1336	        # on disk, so a concurrent in-process LedgerStore construction cannot
1337	        # scan a half-written promotion.
1338	        with self._recovery_lock:
1339	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
1340	                prefix=SNAPSHOT_PREFIX,
1341	                suffix=f".gen{next_generation}",
1342	                dir=directory,
1343	            )
1344	            promoted = False
1345	            try:
1346	                with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
1347	                    json.dump(data, fh, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
1348	                    fh.flush()
1349	                    os.fsync(fh.fileno())
1350	                os.replace(tmp_path, self.path)
1351	                promoted = True
1352	                self._fsync_dir(directory)
1353	                # Promotion is durable: now publish the prospective derived
1354	                # views and advance the generation, together and last, so a
1355	                # successful write is the only thing that changes memory.
1356	                self.tx_index = next_index
1357	                self.accounts = next_accounts
1358	                self.generation = next_generation
1359	            finally:
1360	                if not promoted and os.path.exists(tmp_path):
1361	                    # Promotion never happened: drop the half-written candidate so
1362	                    # it cannot masquerade as a recoverable snapshot. A candidate
1363	                    # written and fsynced *before* a crash during replace survives
1364	                    # precisely because that crash skips this cleanup.
1365	                    try:
1366	                        os.unlink(tmp_path)
1367	                    except OSError:
1368	                        pass

1375	        except OSError:

1377	        try:
1378	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
1379	        except OSError:
1380	            pass
1381	        finally:
1382	            os.close(dir_fd)
